binary64_model.absolute_subnormal_allowance: eta=2^-1075; a real bound represented exactly as a rational, never rounded to binary64 zero.
binary64_model.addition_recurrence: Given centers x,y and radii ex,ey, b=ex+ey; e_add=b+u*(|x+y|+b)+eta. For subtraction replace y by -y. Negation and copies are exact.
binary64_model.contraction_order_robustness: For a sum of n products of d exact operands, using each term once with binary64 multiplication/addition in any binary summation tree, at most d*n meaningful roundings is a conservative normal-range count. FMA is covered by this looser envelope. It does not cover arbitrary algebraic rewrites, omitted/duplicated terms, non-IEEE modes, or compiler transformations lacking this operation-graph association.
binary64_model.division_recurrence: Require |y|>ey. q=x/y; b=(ex+|q|*ey)/(|y|-ey); e_div=b+u*(|q|+b)+eta. Division by 2 is exact only when its result is representable without underflow rounding; otherwise include the eta recurrence.
binary64_model.gamma: gamma_k=k*u/(1-k*u), k*u<1. The simple gamma formulas below additionally require normal-range intermediates (or exact zero); otherwise use the additive-eta recurrences, not the gamma-only bound.
binary64_model.independent_reference_option: A tiny software round-to-nearest oracle implemented with integer/Fraction bit arithmetic can certify a specified operation graph and its range without trusting host float arithmetic. To cover unknown summation order, use the conservative operand envelope or an interval hull over permitted trees; never assume one selected tree matches c_einsum.
binary64_model.interval_centers_and_radii: All operands are exact saved dyadics. Centers and nonnegative radii are exact rationals. Bounds are computed from inputs/operation counts before comparing observed defects; no fitted multiplier, observed-defect allowance, or tolerance floor.
binary64_model.one_rounding_theorem: For correctly rounded round-to-nearest binary64 with gradual underflow and finite result, |RN(x)-x| <= u*|x|+eta. Exact overflow/domain boundaries must be checked; flush-to-zero is not covered.

main_conclusion: An operand-only error budget plus exact-rational comparison of the saved captures is a cheap finite-input certification route. The existing diagnostic alone cannot distinguish rounding from an arbitrary stage defect. Installed source metadata does not establish a universal compiled-kernel/pow rounding theorem. A successful independent-budget comparison would bound data error for these 43 inputs and show consistency with the declared model; it cannot uniquely prove the causal origin of a defect.
